reviews.author: internal-review-repo
reviews.body:
Not approved at 5f97770cb920 (built-from checked). Full record: reviews/v1-paper-repo-pr7.md in internal-review-repo (1abb0bad0812). Checked: all tables rebuild from code/results identically except Table 9; ~20 numbers match the CSVs; method text matches bpred/core.py; reserved-paper handling fine (cited paper is on the starter list; exposure disclosed).

### must
M1 (presentation/report). Appendix Figure 5 (design x estimator heat map, `fig4_ablation.pdf`, PDF p.12) overflows the page: it runs over the page number, the x-axis labels are clipped, the "interpolation"/"extrapolation" panel labels overlap, and its caption is absent from the built PDF (the log places the float on p.12, the caption text is not in the PDF; no "Figure 5:" caption exists). Section 5.3 and contribution 1 cite this figure. Answer: size the figure to the 5.5 x ~8 in text block, put it in a float that keeps the caption (check the built PDF for "Figure 5:" and the axis labels), re-check all appendix floats.
M2 (analysis / report). The delivered package cannot regenerate Table 9's paired-ratio column or the text values 0.94 [0.92,0.95], 0.95 [0.94,0.96], 1.09 [1.08,1.11]: `inner50/paired_vs_main.csv` is not in `code/results/` and no script in `code/scripts/` writes it (rebuild prints "--" in that column). The task requires every table to be reproducible by the shipped code. Answer: ship the script and CSV (experiment-repo a464a38 has the analysis) and copy them into `paper-repo` `code/`.
M3 (figtab / report). The script map does not match the paper: `figures/README.md` and `tables/captions.md` call the primary table Table 2, the ablation Fig. 4, ceiling Fig. 5, ordering Fig. 6, msrc Fig. 5b; the paper has Table 1, Fig. 5, Fig. 4, Fig. 7, Fig. 6, and Table 2 is the data audit. Appendix D points readers to that map. Answer: map by the paper's numbers. Also remove world-internal names ("experiment-repo", "analysis role") from the anonymised supplement (`code/REPRO_NOTES.md`, script docstrings).
M4 (report). The data sources and benchmarks are not cited: HELM (Liang et al.), Open LLM Leaderboard v2 (Fourrier et al.), MMLU-Pro and the other benchmarks' papers are on the starter list or are the objective's named data; checklist item 12 says the licences are "those of the Open LLM Leaderboard and HELM" without naming or citing them. Answer: cite each source and benchmark, state licences as checked. The reference list has 32 entries against the venue's recorded 45-70; add the IRT/2PL and k-means/survey-sampling references the method relies on (e.g. Lord, Baker; Hájek/Horvitz-Thompson), and the closest evaluation-efficiency work a reviewer would expect.
M5 (report). Section 5.1-5.2 read as a record of the study: 5.1 is two paragraphs carrying about 60 numbers, post-hoc diagnostics (larger-gap inner split, strong k-means, top-10/50%, 2%, HELM vs leaderboard) and repeated "chosen after the outcomes" qualifiers; the reader cannot find the claim. Answer: one claim per subsection with a figure/table that carries it and 3-5 numbers; move the diagnostics and secondary endpoints to the appendix tables that already hold them, one pointer sentence each; state the selection caveat once.
M6 (for `final`; does not hold `release`, since every claim about anchors/tinyBenchmarks/metabench is already scoped to "our re-implementation"). Baseline fidelity: the anchor, tinyBenchmarks-style and metabench-style methods are own re-implementations (light k-means, own IRT fitter), unvalidated against any published implementation; a referee will ask whether the anchor result (not better than uniform) is an artefact. Answer: run the public anchor-points and tinyBenchmarks code (independent public repositories, not the reserved paper) on at least the seven leaderboard benchmarks in interpolation and extrapolation, or reproduce a published number with the re-implementation; report both.
M7 (release scope, for the record). The recalibrated estimator and the 100-draw per-target run are still computing; the paper does not claim them. This is the remaining work, not a finding against v1; `final` must carry them or state what was attempted.

### may
m1. Several explanations are left untested though cheap: why ridge extrapolates better than logistic predictors; the centred vs uncentred Brier explanation of the ceiling gap (5.4). Test or cut.
m2. Contribution 4 (ordering) and 5.3 (design vs estimator) rest on appendix Figs. 5 and 7; the venue says critical evidence should not live only in the appendix. A compact ordering panel in the main text, or the key cells of the heat map, would fix it.
m3. Intervals reflect target-family sampling only; a bootstrap over benchmarks (13, not independent) would show the uncertainty of the geometric means. The paper discloses this.
m4. Appendix Fig. 6 (M sources) script warns `anchor|irt-plugin` is omitted; fine, but the caption's "not run for this block" should say so for that cell too.

I re-checked against results/primary.csv and results/twopct/primary.csv: balanced x calibrated regression plain-mean 0.95 [0.93,0.97] vs stratified; balanced x difference IRT 0.96 [0.93,0.99] (extrap, vs strat); extrap10 best 0.70 [0.68,0.72]; 2% best difference cell 0.69 [0.67,0.70] / 0.87 [0.85,0.89] of stratified, IRT model alone 1.36 vs uniform in extrapolation; CAT 1.04 [0.91,1.10]. All match. The paper states neither the recalibrated estimator, the two-phase design nor the 100-draw runs as run; that is correct, those jobs are still computing and their results will need a text revision in a later version.
